audit_findings.title: Capitalized ERP cash spending may bypass the owner-earnings deduction
audit_findings.magnitude: $38.2 million in FY2025, equal to 19.4% of the $196.5 million anchor; $13.3 million was spent in H1 2026 and $25.0 million is expected for FY2026
audit_findings.mechanism: Capitalized cloud-implementation payments reduce equity cash flow but may be absent from OE when only PP&E maintenance capital expenditure is deducted.
audit_findings.evidence: In addition, we invested $38.2 million and $12.6 million for capitalized implementation costs associated with the integration, configuration and customization of this new global ERP platform during the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The cash spending and capitalization are demonstrated, but its omission from the anchor is unresolved because no OE reconciliation was supplied. If omitted, the FY2025 amount is large relative to the anchor and could materially reduce the valuation, although some ERP spending may be temporary rather than perpetual.
audit_findings.action: Trace capitalized cloud-implementation additions through the FY2025 OE calculation and cash-flow adjustments, then rerun the valuation with the verified recurring maintenance component deducted and temporary implementation spending separately normalized.

audit_findings.title: The anchor may retain a material noncash deconsolidation gain
audit_findings.magnitude: $20.9 million, equal to 10.6% of the $196.5 million anchor, before symmetric normalization of other one-offs
audit_findings.mechanism: A noncash gain retained in the earnings numerator raises anchor OE and every projected operating cash flow.
audit_findings.evidence: As a result of this deconsolidation, we recognized a non-cash gain of $20.9 million during the year ended December 31, 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: Recognition of the $20.9 million noncash gain is demonstrated; whether the OE calculation removed it is unresolved. Its size is material relative to the anchor. The net correction cannot be inferred without also normalizing the filed $17.0 million debt-extinguishment loss and other genuine one-offs consistently.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the anchor from net income to OE line by line, remove the deconsolidation gain if retained, apply tax-consistent and symmetric treatment to the debt-extinguishment loss and other one-offs, and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Underfunded retirement obligations may impose cash costs beyond normalized OE
audit_findings.magnitude: $74.37 million net funded deficit at December 31, 2025, equal to $1.22 per diluted share and 2.6% of the $2.827 billion base equity value; expected 2026 pension contributions are $14.0 million
audit_findings.mechanism: Incremental funding above pension expense would reduce OE; alternatively, an uncovered funded deficit could be deducted in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company expects to make pension contributions of approximately $14.0 million during 2026 based on current assumptions as of December 31, 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The funded deficit and expected contribution are demonstrated, but no incremental OE omission is demonstrated because pension expense is already embedded in earnings and the $14.0 million contribution is not compared with same-period expense. Even deducting the entire net funded deficit directly from the bridge would reduce base value only from $46.44 to about $45.22 per share, leaving it far below the $86.88 market price.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile 2026 pension and postretirement expense, contributions and benefit payments. Document whether any recurring contribution excess is absent from OE; rerun only if that reconciliation identifies a separately unrecognized recurring cash burden.

audit_findings.title: Parent earnings may be combined with consolidated cash-flow add-backs
audit_findings.magnitude: $12.456 million FY2024 NCI loss gap, equal to 5.5% of FY2024 OE, and $1.385 million FY2025 NCI loss gap, equal to 0.7% of the anchor; FY2016 effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Combining parent-attributable income with consolidated depreciation, capital spending or other adjustments mixes economic claims and can distort historical OE and its trend.
audit_findings.evidence: The financial results and position of noncontrolling interests are included in the Company’s consolidated financial statements.
audit_findings.explanation: The claim-basis inconsistency in the affected history is a demonstrated construction problem, but its valuation magnitude and direction are unresolved because the NCI shares of depreciation, capital spending and other OE adjustments were not supplied. The latest-year gap is small, while the unquantified FY2016 correction could affect the historical trend even though the current anchor is the lower FY2025 actual rather than the $257 million trend estimate.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild FY2016, FY2024 and FY2025 on one consistent basis—either parent-attributable OE with allocated adjustments or consolidated OE with an explicit NCI claim—and recompute the trend and anchor-selection test.

audit_findings.title: The 2025 anchor predates a material footwear joint-venture structure
audit_findings.mechanism: The post-anchor structure may alter future OE through sourcing prices, equity or loan funding, distributions and consolidation effects, and may create an additional bridge claim.
audit_findings.evidence: The primary purpose of ACL FootJoy, in which the Company has a 40 % interest, with the remaining 60 % owned by Myre, is to source raw materials for, and contract for the manufacture and production of, footwear in Vietnam, under trademarks and brand names owned by Acushnet Company at one or more factories owned and/or controlled by Myre and/or its affiliates (the “Footwear Factories”), including the Long An Factory.
audit_findings.explanation: The structural change is demonstrated, but an adverse valuation effect is not. The June 2026 filing states that Acushnet is the primary beneficiary and consolidates ACL FootJoy, reducing the risk that only its 40% legal ownership is represented in reported results. It also reports a $7.5 million non-interest-bearing JV borrowing and only $0.761 million of consolidated NCI, while additional Acushnet funding is permitted but not legally required. The record does not isolate the JV's margins, transfer-pricing effects or future capital needs, so materiality remains unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Obtain ACL FootJoy standalone H1 2026 cash flows, consolidation eliminations, purchase-pricing terms, guarantees and capital commitments; reconcile these to consolidated OE and rerun the perimeter only if cash attributable to common shareholders differs materially from consolidated results.

audit_findings.title: Redeemable NCI is omitted from the equity bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $1.18 million net carrying amount at June 30, 2026, equal to about $0.02 per diluted share and 0.04% of base equity value; even treating the $4.4 million minority-shareholder loan as unrecoverable produces a $5.58 million claim, about $0.09 per share and 0.20% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Any net redemption obligation not captured in OE is a senior equity claim that should be deducted in the bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Redeemable noncontrolling interests are those noncontrolling interests which are or may become redeemable at a fixed or determinable price on a fixed or determinable date, at the option of the holder, or upon occurrence of an event.
audit_findings.explanation: The bridge omission is demonstrated, but the filed net amount is too small to affect the valuation conclusion. Even the conservative computed amount assuming no recovery of the offsetting shareholder loan is immaterial compared with the $2.827 billion base equity value and the $40.44 per-share gap between base value and market price.
audit_findings.action: Confirm the current contractual redemption value and collectability of the $4.4 million shareholder loan, then deduct the verified net claim in the next bridge update.
